### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d78a0bda07c4bed2e3b71e051ac5db2632b82741`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os lint (command, 30 pages)`, `os validate (command, 53 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **25** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d78a0bda07c4bed2e3b71e051ac5db2632b82741` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8647e2d4b860e859f958f604110b88ed4e3047cc` — the merge of head `dd6fa5537450a9b13d982abead4b9e543a39725b` into base `d78a0bda07c4bed2e3b71e051ac5db2632b82741`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8647e2d4b860e859f958f604110b88ed4e3047cc && git checkout 8647e2d4b860e859f958f604110b88ed4e3047cc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d78a0bda07c4bed2e3b71e051ac5db2632b82741 dd6fa5537450a9b13d982abead4b9e543a39725b && git checkout -B drift-repro d78a0bda07c4bed2e3b71e051ac5db2632b82741 && git merge --no-ff dd6fa5537450a9b13d982abead4b9e543a39725b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d78a0bda07c4bed2e3b71e051ac5db2632b82741
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d78a0bda07c4bed2e3b71e051ac5db2632b82741` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dd6fa5537450a9b13d982abead4b9e543a39725b`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #20583 (body and all ten comments, governed by `5884692257`, `5886671384`, `5916544096`, `5916638647` and the newest `os-dev-report` `5918429389`); #20618 and its PR #20651 (`packages/spec/src/stack-provenance.ts`, `stack.zod.ts` at this head); PR #20617; PR #20926's body, file list and net diff `cb4c31dd52..dd6fa55374` (6 files, +148 / −14); the check-runs on this head, collapsed latest-per-name. The dispatch order and the dispatching seat's own conclusions were not inputs.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept set: unchanged. Public surface: no export added or removed; no `--json` key added or removed; no text-face byte changes. What changes is the CONTENT of the existing `conversions` array on the refusal path of `os validate --json`, `os build --json` and `os lint --json`, from `[]` to the ADR-0087 conversions the refusing producer applied. Each judged below.

**(a) The fold reads the producer's own record, unwrapped, exactly once — RIGHT.**
- `stackConversionsOf(error)` (`packages/spec/src/stack-provenance.ts:259`) answers the frozen `ConversionNotice[]` that a value carries as its OWN property under `Symbol.for('objectstack.stack.conversions')`, and only when the value is a marked stack or an `instanceof Error`; otherwise the frozen empty record. The only writers are `markStackProvenance` and `markRefusalConversions`, both internal to spec (`stack.zod.ts:3800` re-exports `hasStackProvenance` and `stackConversionsOf` only; `index.ts` does `export * from './stack.zod'` and never names `stack-provenance`). `markRefusalConversions` is reached solely through `withRefusalConversions` in `defineStack` and `composeStacks`, and only for `instanceof StackRefusalError`. So the three catch-alls read what the producer recorded at its throw. No second `normalizeStackInput` pass was added anywhere, and nothing reads stderr: the two channels the seat answer `5886671384` declined are absent from the diff.
- `loadConfig` (`packages/cli/src/utils/config.ts:589-669`) rethrows the stamped refusal untouched: `resolveConfigPath` then a bare `bundleRequire({ filepath, external })` with no `try`, so the config module's throw leaves as the same object. The only errors config.ts constructs itself are `ConfigRefusalError` (no `code`) and a plain `Error` for a missing default export; neither is stamped. Leaving config.ts unedited was the correct reading of the claim's conditional line.
- Double report: in all three doors `loadConfig` is the first statement of the `try`; step 1b (`conversionNotices.push(...loaded.stackConversions)`, validate.ts:243, compile.ts:277, lint.ts:971) and step 2's pass come after it. A load that throws never reaches 1b or 2, so the catch-all is the list's only filler on that run. A throw after 1b can carry a record only if a producer runs after load, and none does: at this head `git grep` over `packages/cli/src` (non-test) finds `defineStack(` / `composeStacks(` only in prose, scaffold templates (`init.ts`, `create.ts`) and comments; `packages/lint/src` and `packages/objectql/src` hit tests, strings and comments only. The CLI's own refusals (`StackProvenanceMissingError` in `stack-provenance-refusal.ts:42`, `ConfigRefusalError`) are plain `Error` subclasses, never stamped. `os build` inherits compile's catch. A composed stack: `composeStacks` stamps its refusal with `composedConversions(stacks)`, a `Set` over identity-frozen notices (one application once); and when an input `defineStack` refuses inside the array literal, that refusal is thrown before `composeStacks` runs and carries its own record only (first stamp wins, `markRefusalConversions` returns an already-stamped error unchanged). One record, folded once, on every path.
- A non-refusal or unstamped throw yields `[]`: a plain `Error`, an esbuild `BuildFailure`, the CLI's refusals, the bare zod error from `composeStacks`' options parse (not a `StackRefusalError`), a forged plain object carrying the key without the mark (`isStampedRefusal` requires `instanceof Error`), and an heir of a stamped refusal (own-property test). The canonical-then-refuse controls pin the empty answer on all three doors.

**(b) Text face unchanged, fold inside the `--json` branch — RIGHT, and consistent with the direction.** Triage's direction (`5884692257`) reads 「carries the conversions it applied into the refusal's `--json`」; the card body names the loss as 「loses the conversions from `--json`」; the claim's surface says the same. The text face of a refusing run is byte-identical before and after this diff: the producer's own warn-once stderr line still carries the notice there, as it did. On the success path the door additionally prints the folded record in its warning block at step 2; on the refusal path it prints the refusal alone. That asymmetry pre-dates this PR and the direction did not ask to close it; `--json` is the complete channel. It is a boundary to note, not a defect (see ③).

**(c) Payload shape — RIGHT.** The emitted object literals are untouched by the diff: validate `valid, error, code and httpStatus via errorCodeFields, warnings, conversions, duration`; compile `success, error, the same carriers, warnings, conversions`; lint `error, the same carriers, conversions`. Only the `conversionNotices` binding's content changes, and only when the caught error is a stamped refusal. `code` is read by `errorCodeFields` off the same error object (the stamp is a non-enumerable symbol property and touches neither `code` nor `httpStatus`); the exits stay `this.exit(1)` / `process.exit(1)`. The new pins assert the envelope per door (`expectCatchAll`: exit 1, `code` `STACK_CAPABILITY_UNKNOWN`, `error` a string, `valid: false` / `success: false`) and `expectExactly` asserts `conversions` by `toEqual` against exactly the one notice, or `[]` for the control — exactly-once, not containment.

**(d) The `validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` row — RIGHT, reason text true.** The closed roster's scan (`callSitesOf`) matches a bare identifier followed by `(` and skips property accesses, so step 1b's `loaded.stackConversions` never reached it and the new bare call `stackConversionsOf(` in both `compile.ts` and `validate.ts` does; the unit run at `649236e024` went red on exactly that name. `NOT_A_GATE` under its own reason key is the right ledger: the call raises no finding and refuses nothing, the refusal was thrown and the conversions applied by the producer before it runs, and the exit is 1 whether it answers the record or `[]`. It is not a gate (not `SHARED_NON_REGISTRY_GATES`), not presentation, and both commands (and `lint.ts`) call it, so `parityGapBetween` has nothing to report and `no ledger entry is stale` sees it live. Each clause of the reason text checks against the code.

**(e) Changeset `@objectstack/cli` `patch` — RIGHT; claims nothing undelivered.** The three doors, the refusal beside the conversions, exactly once, `[]` for a refusal whose source needed no conversion and for any other load failure, no key added, exit / `error` / `code` unchanged, text face unchanged: each is in the diff and pinned (the six new door rows; the nightly source-scan pins hold the load-throw `[]` rows and every exit reading the one sink). `stackConversionsOf(error)` in `@objectstack/spec` is a landed fact (#20651, api-surface `root.json:201`). One wording imprecision, not a false claim: 「a `defineStack` or `composeStacks` call converts a deprecated spelling」 — `composeStacks` converts nothing; its refusal carries what its inputs' `defineStack` calls converted (spec `composedConversions`). The behaviour claimed for it holds by the same fold line and the spec's own pin; it is not pinned at a door. Acceptance note, below.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` with `patch` is right. Under AGENTS.md's changeset rule the declaration answers whether the card widens the accept set or expands the public surface (`yes` takes at least `minor`; `(narrowing)` is BREAKING; no arm is written here, which the closed pair allows). This diff accepts and refuses exactly what `main` does (the refusal still throws, exit 1, same `code`), adds and removes no `--json` key, adds no export, and moves no text-face byte; an existing field on a failure path stops answering `[]` for conversions that were applied. That is a bug fix on a released package (card labelled `bug`), the same shape PR #20617 landed under `no` + `patch` with a PASS at-tier record, and PR #20579 before it. A consumer that asserted `conversions: []` on a refusal was asserting the defect, not a contract. `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Each dev `deviations` entry, answered:

1. **Base `165c1d49e3` rather than the dispatch's `cf684c98eb`, and one merge of `main`.** Verified: `cf684c98eb` is an ancestor of `165c1d49e3`, which is `dd7f3c886a`'s parent; the merge `649236e024` has parents `64bf48ddf1` and `cb4c31dd52`; the branch delta before the merge (`165c1d49e3..64bf48ddf1`) and the merge result against `main` (`cb4c31dd52..649236e024`) are byte-identical (5 files, +139 / −14); between `165c1d49e3` and `cb4c31dd52` `main` touched none of the PR's six files; the merge-base with `main` is `cb4c31dd52`. Accepted.
2. **The parity-ledger edit outside the claim's named files.** Forced by the closed roster, which reddened at `649236e024` on the one new bare call; the row is truthful (①d) and is a pin under `packages/cli/test`, inside the claim's 「pins in `packages/cli`」. Accepted; no escalation.
3. **Three nightly-tier `*.e2e.*` files run locally.** Read-only runs of existing source-scan pins that assert on exactly these catch-alls (every exit reads the one sink; a load-throw plain `Error` answers `[]`); nothing edited; extra evidence beyond the per-PR tiers. The verdicts this record cites are the head's check-runs, not those runs. Accepted.
4. **The fold sits inside the `--json` branch only.** Answered at ①(b): consistent with the direction as written. Acceptance note: on a refusal the text face carries the notice only through the producer's warn-once stderr line, so a repeated notice across a composed config is printed once there; `--json` is the complete channel.
5. **The attribution trailer.** The harness reminder named a model in `Co-Authored-By`; AGENTS.md binds the model-free pair and its pre-push hook refuses a model identifier, and AGENTS.md wins. Verified on the head: all four non-merge commits end with `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01VvcEokUG1tvVxkceYfR5XB` and the model-free `Co-authored-by: Claude` line with the noreply address; the merge commit carries no trailer (a merge, as #20617's landing record accepted); no model identifier appears in the diff, the commit messages, the changeset or the PR body; the PR body's footer is the session-URL form.

Anything in the diff that should have been an `out_of_scope_findings` or `open_questions` entry: no. Checked and set aside: `lint.ts`'s `--eval --generator` load failure (`:1385`) emits no `conversions` key — pre-existing, fenced to its own card in its comment, not this door; a composition refusal reaching a door has no door pin (spec pins the stamp; the fold is type-agnostic); the changeset's `composeStacks` wording (①e); the refusal text face (item 4). None is a reproducible defect, a contract violation or an authoring trap; all three belong in Acceptance notes. The card's carry-over (`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` 「Warnings checked」) stays where the card left it.

Check-runs on this head, read from the API and collapsed latest-per-name, converged at 19:56:36Z: 34 names, 31 `success`, 3 `skipped` (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 0 failed or cancelled. The seven required contexts are all `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (six shards and the rollup), `Dogfood Regression Gate` (three shards and the rollup), `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Also `success`: `Check Changeset`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue`, `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the four `Type Check` legs, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Auto Label`, `filter`. The six new door rows run in the per-PR population (`test/stack-conversion-record-door.test.ts` carries no nightly-tier name and spawns the CLI, so it is the queue population's integration project under `Test Core`), which is green on this head.
